people.primary_responsibilities: Leads overall design direction and project delivery for custom residential architecture and integrated interiors, oversees client relationships and fee strategy, and co-manages the studio’s project mix and quality standards.
people.relevant_background: Master of Architecture; licensed architect in North Carolina and South Carolina; 24 years of practice in residential and interior architecture.
people.why_strengthens_business: Ottoline combines deep design experience with local hillside and climate expertise and direct fee-setting authority, so she can both win and deliver the high-caliber projects Marchetti & Fen depends on while maintaining margins and client satisfaction.
people.paragraph: Ottoline Marchetti serves as Principal Architect and co-owner, bringing 24 years of experience in residential and interior architecture plus a Master of Architecture and licensure in both North Carolina and South Carolina. She leads overall design direction and delivery, anchors key client relationships, and sets fee and scope strategy, ensuring that every project benefits from senior-level judgment. Her combination of deep technical expertise, local hillside and climate knowledge, and hands-on involvement in both architecture and interiors gives Marchetti & Fen the credibility and execution capacity to deliver complex custom homes at the standards its positioning and pricing require.

people.primary_responsibilities: Co-leads architectural and interior design for all projects, manages day-to-day studio delivery, and ensures integrated execution from feasibility and site analysis through construction documents.
people.relevant_background: Master of Architecture; licensed architect in North Carolina; 19 years of practice focused on custom residential and commercial fit-out design.
people.why_strengthens_business: Rasheed pairs senior design and licensure with deep familiarity with Marchetti & Fen’s processes, allowing the studio to run multiple overlapping projects while keeping partner-level quality on both architecture and interiors.
people.paragraph: Rasheed Fennimore is Design Director and co-owner, with 19 years of experience, a Master of Architecture, and architectural licensure in North Carolina. He co-leads both the architectural and interior scopes on every project, manages the day-to-day workload of the studio, and keeps design development, documentation, and coordination moving smoothly across overlapping jobs. By combining senior design judgment with close control of project execution, Rasheed enables Marchetti & Fen to maintain a true partner-led model while handling the volume of concurrent residential, interior, and commercial fit-out work that underpins the firm’s revenue goals.

marketing_model_json.marketing_basis_summary:
Business stage & model: Pre-revenue, senior-led, high-fee residential architecture and interiors studio with a small, mixed B2C/B2B client base, local/regional physical sales model, and capacity of ~40 projects/year at an average of ~$53k per project to reach ~$2.1M Year‑1 revenue. Marketing’s job in Year 1 is to generate a modest but high-quality flow of design-committed leads (mostly residential, some commercial), not broad-scale volume.

B2C narrowing (people/customers):
- ACS education segment (~79k adults) is a ceiling across the wider area, not the direct market.
- True target is affluent, design-committed homeowners and near-term homebuilders/renovators in their 40s–60s within Asheville + nearby WNC communities + a bit of SC.
- Within the broader educated adult base, only a small minority will be both: (a) in the top local income/asset tiers or relocating with major equity, and (b) actively planning a custom home or large-scale renovation in the next ~2 years.
- From that, further narrow to those who value high design, want integrated architecture-plus-interiors, and who would realistically consider a two-partner boutique practice at $68k+ architecture and $31k interiors price points.
- Given local scope, the cadence of major residential projects, and the studio’s capacity (~34 residential + ~6 commercial projects), a reachable B2C universe of roughly 360 plausible residential customers in Year 1 is realistic: this includes in‑market and near‑term planners who might encounter the brand via referrals, builders, GBP/search, Instagram, events, and directories.

B2B narrowing (firms):
- CBP basis for the selected NAICS across North Carolina is 23,462 establishments (restaurants, cafés, select food retail, and boutiques). This is a state‑level ceiling, not a local TAM.
- The studio’s realistic Year‑1 geographic reach is Asheville, nearby WNC communities, and some nearby SC, with a strong bias to independent, owner-operated restaurants/cafés and boutiques that: (a) control their own design decisions; (b) are established (older age bands); and (c) are considering a renovation, new concept, or second location.
- Many of the 23,462 establishments are chains, convenience/commodity formats, or outside the practical drive radius and relationship network for a two-partner, relationship-driven studio.
- Anchoring to the feedback and to physical sales coverage, a plausible Year‑1 *reachable* B2B universe is on the order of low dozens to low hundreds. A conservative planning figure of ~60 firms reflects:
  - A subset of independent, design-forward operators in Asheville and key nearby WNC towns (plus a few in adjacent SC) within the relevant NAICS; and
  - The small slice of those who will be in an active or near-term project window during Year 1.
- This keeps the B2B reachable subset as a small, realistic fraction of the 23,462‑establishment statewide CBP base while still leaving room for selective outreach via directories, events, and referrer networks.

Combined reachable_market (planning view only):
- reachable_market is reported as 420 (360 B2C people + 60 B2B firms) as a planning abstraction for entity‑level reach, not a literal homogeneous TAM. Residential homeowners and commercial owner‑operators behave very differently and are addressed via different channels, but for Year‑1 pipeline planning it’s useful to have a combined, order‑of‑magnitude view.

Capture logic & expected units:
- Required Year‑1 units: ~39.6 projects, blended across custom residential architecture, residential interiors packages, and commercial fit‑outs.
- With an expected client count of ~36 entities (e.g., ~30 residential clients and ~6 commercial/hospitality/retail firms) and 39.6 projects, you’re assuming some clients will commission multiple scopes (e.g., architecture plus interiors, or phased scopes), which is realistic given the integrated offer.
- Against a reachable planning universe of 420 entities, 39.6 projects implies a capture_rate_year1 of ~0.094 in *unit* terms: roughly 9.4 project‑units per 100 reachable entities. This is not a 9.4% one-time adoption rate; it reflects that:
  - Only a fraction of reachable entities will be in an active project window.
  - A subset of those will shortlist and meet with the studio.
  - A smaller subset will close; some will purchase multiple scopes, boosting units per client.

Marketing intensity & percent of revenue:
- Channels are targeted and credibility‑heavy: Google Business Profile and search (for relocators/local shortlisting), Instagram (finished work, brand story), LinkedIn (professional referrers), curated local events, builder/professional partnerships, and select directories.
- As a pre‑revenue but senior‑led practice, you lack an established brand under this studio name but have strong personal experience and a clearly differentiated positioning (integrated architecture + interiors, partner‑only delivery, WNC hillside/climate expertise).
- Capacity is limited and fees are high; the goal is quality and price integrity more than raw volume. That supports a disciplined, relationship- and reputation-driven marketing mix rather than heavy paid acquisition.
- For a high-fee, low-volume professional service with local scope, a realistic Year‑1 baseline marketing spend is around 8–15% of revenue. Given the need to launch the brand, build a strong portfolio/web presence, and invest in initial relationship and event visibility, but without national paid media, an 11% baseline is appropriate.

Resulting baseline:
- baseline_marketing_percent: 0.11 (11% of ~$2.1M revenue, or roughly ~$230k in Year‑1 marketing and BD spend across website/brand assets, photography and case studies, search presence, light paid search/IG tests if desired, sponsorships/events, directories, and relationship-building activities).
- This level is sufficient to activate the planned channels, support a high‑quality lead flow within the limited local/near‑regional universe, and credibly fill the ~40‑project Year‑1 capacity without assuming unrealistic market saturation.

operating_model_json.business_description_summary: Marchetti & Fen is a design practice providing full-service custom residential architecture, residential interior design packages, and a smaller line of commercial fit-out design projects. Work is delivered as project-based project engagements on a contract cadence, with fees like $31,000-$68,000 per typical project paid in staged milestones. Fulfillment is handled directly by the two partner-level designers with support from a small in-house studio team, moving projects through feasibility and site analysis, concept design, design development, permit and zoning coordination within the architecture scope, and construction documents, plus interiors or commercial fit-outs as applicable. Projects typically run over multiple months, with several overlapping at once; practical capacity is framed as concurrent active project "slots" (e.g., 3-10 active custom residential projects at full capacity, with typical utilization around  and corresponding 0.19-0.54 projects per week on average). Capacity is primarily constrained by available design and project management labor, not demand or software systems, and the studio focuses on a stable project count while improving pricing and attachment of interiors. Standard professional requirements for an architecture and interior design practice—such as state licensure for architects, business registration as a Partnership, appropriate professional liability and general business insurance, and any applicable local permitting or zoning practice rules—are assumed to be incorporated into operations; exact requirements vary by jurisdiction and should be confirmed with local regulators and advisors.
